checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are blob byte sequences encoding values >= BLS_MODULUS properly rejected at bytes_to_bls_field boundary?

reachability.notes: Directly derived from STRIDE tampering threat on tb-001. Adversary controls blob content and can craft byte sequences near or above BLS_MODULUS.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the bytes_to_bls_field function/boundary in the codebase. 2. Craft blob payloads containing byte sequences that encode field element values equal to BLS_MODULUS. 3. Craft blob payloads containing byte sequences that encode field element values greater than BLS_MODULUS (e.g., BLS_MODULUS + 1, MAX_UINT256). 4. Submit these malformed blobs via P2P and Transaction entry points. 5. Verify that the system explicitly REJECTS these blobs with an appropriate error. 6. Confirm the system does NOT silently reduce values modulo BLS_MODULUS. 7. Test across multiple client implementations to verify consistent rejection behavior. 8. Check for any code paths that might bypass this validation.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0044, Trust Boundary: tb-001, Threat: stride-tampering-tb-001. Silent modular reduction vs. rejection causes consensus divergence across clients.

checklist.title: Verify Blob Submitter Input Sanitization: Does actor-blob-submitter enforce BLS field element bounds before encoding?

reachability.notes: Supporting check for blob-submitter node that feeds into tb-001 boundary.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the actor-blob-submitter component and its input interfaces. 2. Review how blob content is accepted from external sources. 3. Check if any pre-validation occurs before blob reaches bytes_to_bls_field. 4. Verify that malicious blob content cannot bypass submitter-level checks. 5. Test edge cases: blobs with mixed valid/invalid field elements.

checklist.title: Verify Cell Encoder Field Element Handling: Does actor-cell-encoder correctly propagate rejection for invalid field elements?

reachability.notes: Supporting check for cell-encoder node involved in tb-001 boundary processing.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the actor-cell-encoder component in the codebase. 2. Trace how field elements flow from bytes_to_bls_field to cell encoding. 3. Verify that rejection at bytes_to_bls_field properly halts cell encoding. 4. Check for any fallback logic that might continue processing with reduced values. 5. Confirm error propagation is consistent and does not leak partial state.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is O(n^2) complexity of compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs_polynomialcoeff bounded to prevent DoS via blob submission?

reachability.notes: An attacker submitting maximally-sized blobs triggers the O(n^2) proof generation. The FK20 algorithm is recommended for production but may not be implemented in all clients.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the implementation of compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs_polynomialcoeff (SG-019) in the target client. 2. Measure the execution time for proof generation with a single maximum-sized blob (128KB). 3. Calculate the total time required for processing MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK blobs per slot. 4. Compare the total proof generation time against the slot time budget (12 seconds for Ethereum mainnet). 5. Verify that rate-limiting mechanisms exist at the P2P layer to prevent blob flooding. 6. Check if the FK20 algorithm (O(n log n)) is implemented instead of the naive O(n^2) approach. 7. Test resource allocation: can a single blob submission starve other validator operations? 8. Attempt to submit maximum-sized blobs at high frequency via P2P and monitor validator slot production latency.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0045, Trust Boundary: tb-001, Source Invariant: SG-019-INV-003, Source Threat: stride-dos-tb-001. The O(n^2) complexity is particularly dangerous as it amplifies with blob count - processing 6 max-sized blobs could take 36x longer than a single blob. Validators missing slots due to slow proof generation could face slashing penalties.

checklist.title: Verify blob submitter rate limiting prevents proof generation DoS

reachability.notes: Supporting check for rate limiting mechanisms at the blob submission boundary.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify rate limiting implementation for blob submissions in the P2P layer. 2. Verify per-peer blob submission limits are enforced. 3. Check that global blob queue limits prevent memory exhaustion. 4. Test that malicious peers cannot bypass rate limits via connection multiplexing. 5. Verify that the blob mempool has bounded size and eviction policies. 6. Confirm that blob validation (including proof generation) is performed before propagation to prevent amplification attacks.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0045, Supporting check for actor-blob-submitter. Rate limiting is the primary defense if O(n^2) complexity cannot be reduced.

checklist.title: Verify proof generator resource allocation prevents slot deadline violations

reachability.notes: Supporting check for proof generator resource management.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify how proof generation is scheduled relative to other validator duties. 2. Check if proof generation has a timeout mechanism that prevents indefinite blocking. 3. Verify that proof generation failures are handled gracefully without crashing the validator. 4. Test that blob proof generation can be preempted for higher-priority tasks (attestation, block production). 5. Measure CPU and memory consumption during maximum-load proof generation. 6. Verify that the validator can still produce timely attestations while generating proofs.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0045, Supporting check for actor-proof-generator. Even with rate limiting, proper resource allocation is needed to ensure proof generation doesn't starve other validator operations.
